 Adonais did indeed receive predictable critical broadsides from the Tory critics it
directly addressed. Blackwood’s x (1821) 696–700 jeered and scoffed, in an article by George
Croly, whose own work is singled out as amongst the ‘illustrious obscure’ in the Preface
to Adonais (see notes). The Literary Gazette more solemnly denounced the ‘atrocities’ in
the poem, while dwelling mainly on what it takes to be its nonsensical character (255 (8
December 1821) 772–3). But the version of the poem published in the Literary Chronicle
on 1 December 1821 was accompanied by a supportive introduction, and in the months
and years following S.’s death Adonais did not attract hostility. Sustained critical accounts
of the poem are, however, virtually non-existent right up to the end of the nineteenth cen-
tury, although the marginal comments by S.’s friend Taaffe on his copy show that, amongst
